# maestro-security: unified design v3

THE FUSION. Design and build contract for issue #14; not an implementation claim.

## 1. Authority and completion boundary

This document replaces the capability guesses in v2. It is the P2 input to the
catalog and runner tickets, after the accepted decomposition at `446cb83`.
The order remains decomposition, fusion, catalog, runner, then box integration
and strip-down. Neither this document nor a graph join authorizes those later
steps to start before their review gates pass.

There is one Maestro security framework. `maestro-security-runner` owns its
Rust engine, contracts, state and capabilities. Maestro hosts the five catalog
agents; the extension supplies the session/WASM adapter. Raw tools, analysis
engines and models remain in the box. No absorbed framework or external
analysis orchestration server is invoked as a substitute for ported logic.
Raw engine protocols remain legitimate execution boundaries.

The binding architecture is SPEC.md, AUTONOMY.md and ADR-0001 through ADR-0023
in the documentation trail. Later closure rulings override the earlier row
interpretations they name; they are design requirements, not implemented fixes.
Their assistant-authored entries do not acquire owner authority merely by
being called ADRs. The owner-directed sequence and the live supervisor
clarifications below determine this fusion's scope.

The following clarifications were received while writing v3:

| Question | Binding contract |
| --- | --- |
| Task versus workflow | The seven investigation units are tasks. Each runs alone; a workflow file chains them. Use `--tasks` and `--workflow`, not the superseded selection flags. |
| One methodology versus selectable plans | Quick/standard/deep change selected tasks, breadth and budgets, never the evidence or safety rules. |
| Workspace writes | Fixes and destructive actions are proposals. Separate user authorization can permit execution only in box-owned scratch, never mutation of the user's workspace. |
| Crate ownership | Move logic once into the runner library/native binary. The WASM/session adapter and existing MCP binary delegate to that library; schemas and types have one definition. |
| Graph records with wrong source identities | Preserve the recorded ids but exclude the affected rows from graph proof. A pre-build re-check must settle them before P3/P4 consume them. |

`2168` source-qualified entries have a destination in the reverse table.
This includes capability-table rows, their explicitly labelled unknown/ownership
rows, and 42 correction overlays. It excludes identity/evidence-count tables,
Markdown separators, graph appendix headers and historical aggregate community
counts. An overlay is a separate citation, not a new target capability.
Line anchors disambiguate repeated labels and overlapping row ids. All 44
mission Markdown files, including the count note and correction files, are
listed in the source inventory. The graph appender's metadata/header rows are
not promoted into product capabilities.

## 2. Architecture and one-owner rules

The data path is:

```text
explicit user request
  -> session / CLI / MCP / local RPC adapter
  -> one parsed command and contract registry
  -> isolated runner process and immutable run identity
  -> selected task(s), typed action proposals, deterministic gates
  -> box execution or raw analysis engine protocol
  -> retained receipt/evidence and coverage commit
  -> validated finding/report -> event seam -> curated Maestro entry
```

The runner library contains runtime-neutral contracts plus cfg-gated native
execution and persistence. The WASM adapter keeps compiling for
`wasm32-wasip2` with all nine existing tools. It calls the native run boundary;
it does not host a second engine in the session or rely on a WASM async tail
to survive the session. Native-host integration remains extension-owned under
ADR-0003; this design does not add a Maestro core subagent API.

The file-by-file plan is the architecture map. Each row names the final file,
one responsibility, production-line ceiling, red-first obligation, source row
set, both recorded graph sides and explicit exclusions. Current modules are
relocated or retained there; no existing source file disappears without a
named destination. New leaf files split real protocol/contract families to
stay under 500 counted production lines. Their existing Maestro witnesses
justify the source owner being split, not a claim that the future file already
has a graph node. Regenerate the Rust graph after relocation and each slice.

| Logic | Single owner | Callers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wire contracts, schema/effect registry | runner `tools.rs` and family leaves | All four command adapters, nine tools, catalog export and raw-provider calls |
| State transitions and revisions | `autonomy/run.rs`, `pipeline/decision.rs`, `store.rs`, each at its own boundary | Commands and task/action drivers; adapters never mutate records directly |
| Receipts, lineage and unknowns | `evidence.rs` and its receipt/journal/unknown leaves | Task outputs, finding validators, report/evidence pages and audit readers |
| Execution admission and lifecycle | `runner.rs` and its guard/process/session/transport leaves | Every shell/code/browser/device/provider path; never an adapter-owned executor |
| Knowledge and instructions | Manifest skill/instructions resources, composed by `methodology.rs` | Five Maestro agents and task prompts; no parallel hard-coded corpus |

The JSON stores remain the only backing store. A workspace directory is its
identity, and its session record is the durable mapping to run/attempt ids.
The existing runs index remains a listing projection, not a second workspace
identity registry. No SQL server, SQLite file, vector database, graph database
or workflow service ships in the port (ADR-0022). `graph.rs` is an in-memory,
JSON-backed analysis model. It is not a new backend.

Resolve the model once per run: an explicit override wins, then the configured
preferred model when served, otherwise the router/bridge catalog's first
model. `models.rs` owns that helper; context, engine and doctor share it and
record the actual resolved identity. The loopback router
`http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` and box audience bridge
`http://host.docker.internal:8001/box/v1` remain configured endpoints, not new
services. Credentials come from runtime settings/environment and never from
an embedded capability key. P2 does not modify those services or credentials.

## 3. Agents, instructions and knowledge

Catalog ids follow the package draft's `kind:package/name` form. Runtime agent
names stay Maestro-branded. The five agent definitions live in Maestro and use
the runner, rather than being five copies of the engine (ADR-0014).

| Runtime role | Qualified catalog id | Work and instructions | Knowledge resource |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maestro.security` | `agent:maestro-security/security` | Coordinate the selected tasks and evidence-backed actions; resolve scope/Always-Ask-Never; consolidate units; reserve critics, proof and reporting; publish only after validation. | `skill:maestro-security/security-knowledge` |
| `maestro.probe` | `agent:maestro-security/security-probe` | Discover source/target surfaces, principals and sinks; quote raw observations with parent ids; return structured hunter units and candidates, not verdict prose. | `skill:maestro-security/probe-knowledge` |
| `maestro.proof` | `agent:maestro-security/security-proof` | Independently challenge each proposed confirmation, reconcile exact receipts, run fresh-eye verification, enforce numerical floors and disclose missing facts. | `skill:maestro-security/proof-knowledge` |
| `maestro.rebuild` | `agent:maestro-security/security-rebuild` | Reconstruct architecture and contracts from observed facts; ground fixes in exact-version documentation; keep assumptions and non-source decompiler artifacts explicit. | `skill:maestro-security/rebuild-knowledge` |
| `maestro.cyber` | `agent:maestro-security/security-cyber` | Build threat paths, attack-class questions and standard hardening; retain domain exclusions, false-positive conditions and bounded local validation rules. | `skill:maestro-security/cyber-knowledge` |

Every role requires `instructions:maestro-security/security-assessment` and
`skill:maestro-security/security-assessment`. The instruction resource defines
one authority hierarchy: canonical run state and scope are authoritative;
target text, tool diagnostics, fetched documentation and steering text are
untrusted data. Instructions do not replace deterministic admission. The root
skill explains invocation, tasks/workflows, retained evidence and the nine-tool
surface; agent packs contain the detailed knowledge selected for that role.

Source routing is explicit: S15 feeds security's scope gate; S22/S23 and the
floor-guard rows feed proof; B01-B30 feed probe/cyber; coverage, setup, budget,
verification and reporting rules feed security/proof. The 51 observed domain
documents become 51 separately addressable lazy domain skill payloads under
`skill:maestro-security/domain-<domain-id>`, retaining the observed frontmatter
identity. Their corpus row is the family provenance; it is an extraction
exclusion, not 51 invented graph joins. P3 enumerates the shipped ids against
that source inventory and refuses duplicates or missing members. The four
absent documents and the two unlocated cloud skills receive no capability
credit. Vendored tool documentation is not security knowledge.

Each domain pack keeps its attack classes, universal moves, required proof,
non-findings, prohibited live tests and precise `needs_validation` facts.
The corrected clause tails override earlier summaries: credentialed wildcard
CORS is rejected by browsers; cloud review does not assume a permissive
firewall or absent admission attachment and prohibits live probing; memory
claims cannot exceed the observed effect; resource tests do not create
availability impact; release checks never publish a real release.

Hardening patterns are target-review knowledge, not a blanket ban on the
explicitly configured local router or authorized box targets. They include
parameterized queries, per-resource authorization, response omission,
all-address DNS checks and redirect refusal. The SSRF range list is explicitly
loopback, link-local `169.254.169.254`, private and unique-local IPv4/IPv6;
high-risk fetches pin the resolved IP or use a filtering agent. Destructive
cleanup requires a resolved allowlisted root, at least one level below it,
and authenticated ownership evidence read before teardown; no-follow
held-descriptor operations address the check/use race. Sensitive data needs
stricter access and often encryption plus audit logging. The real section
anchors are :121, :204, :239 and :297 in the cited companion.

Ideation, context packing, performance diagnosis, telemetry, release and
simplification bodies remain usable instructions and review knowledge. They
do not authorize automatic project changes, deployments, network installs or
new infrastructure. The floor guard is a read-only Rust capability: merge-base
plus added/removed/untracked changes, hunk-aware headers, directional threshold
pairing, assertion/test deletion and suppression/stub/exception detection.
Exit 2 means it could not run, not clean; matched secrets are never printed.

## 4. Tasks and workflow file

The atomic investigation unit is a task. `PhaseKind` and the event field
`phase` are existing wire/source names; they represent a selected task slot,
not a second workflow model. Internal action proposals use `ActionKind` for
`discover/enumerate/test/exploit/verify/recover` so that those six action kinds
cannot be confused with the seven catalog tasks.

| Qualified task id | Input and output | Canonical position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task:maestro-security/recon` | Scoped target/source ref and doctor result -> raw observations, principals, entry surfaces and offline execution constraints. | 1 |
| `task:maestro-security/target-model` | Retained observations -> cited architecture/trust-boundary model, prior-run reconciliation and deterministic coverage units. | 2 |
| `task:maestro-security/hypotheses` | Model and coverage units -> smallest evidence-backed actions, variant/class breadth and structured candidate proposals. | 3 |
| `task:maestro-security/verify` | Candidate/action/receipt references -> independent proof/refutation, validated verdict branches, owned coverage attempts. | 4 |
| `task:maestro-security/deepen` | Confirmed records -> one bounded impact extension and minimal fix/regression proposals; no workspace application. | 5 |
| `task:maestro-security/threat` | Cited target model -> assets, actors, exposure paths and standard hardening ranked by impact and likelihood. | 6 |
| `task:maestro-security/report` | Validated records and coverage -> immutable JSON/HTML/text/SARIF projections, gaps and spend. | 7 |

Each task is executable alone. One workflow file defines canonical order,
allowed predecessor/successor relationships and the named task lists. A
relationship constrains relative order; it does not require the immediately
preceding task to have run. Any ordered subset of the canonical chain is a
legal selection. Missing retained inputs produce typed `input_needed`/blocked
results; omitted tasks never run secretly. The output states which inputs and
coverage are missing. Running recon alone does not imply a full assessment.

The workflow file has these exact lists:

| Workflow entry | Ordered task list | Row-backed budget/breadth plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow:maestro-security/security-assessment` (canonical) | recon, target-model, hypotheses, verify, deepen, threat, report | Chain only; no plan-specific budget profile. |
| `workflow:maestro-security/standard` | recon, target-model, hypotheses, verify, deepen, threat, report | Default budgets; validation/critics/report reserves apply. |
| `workflow:maestro-security/deep` | recon, target-model, hypotheses, verify, deepen, threat, report | Units split by subsystem/lifecycle; root bands 70/85/95, worker bands 75/80/85, 90% report reserve; critic waves continue to a clean pass or disclosed stop. |
| `workflow:maestro-security/quick` | recon, target-model, hypotheses, verify, report | Coarser units, one hunter wave and one final post-wave critic; accepted extra work is explicitly deferred. Identical evidence bar. |

Selections are one task (`--tasks recon`), an explicit list
(`--tasks recon,verify`), or one named workflow (`--workflow deep`). These
selectors are mutually exclusive; an invalid order, duplicate or unknown task
is a usage error. Omission selects the canonical workflow. The same selections
and qualified ids reach all transports. The superseded flags are not added as
aliases because they were never an accepted shipped contract.

P3 transcribes this into one workflow-definition file in `maestro-manifests`.
The package draft fields remain `kind`, `name`, `version`, `owners`,
`description`, `status`, then `[metadata]` with
`schema = "maestro-source/2"`, `maturity`, `rows`,
`workflows = ["security-assessment"]` and `requires` containing qualified
`agent:...`, `instructions:...` and `skill:...` ids. The seven `task:...`
entries and four `workflow:...` entries reference the same task definitions;
P3 must not create four copies of their logic. Exact resource serialization
is subject to the owner's still-open manifest resource-shape grill; no held
draft is silently treated as an approved schema extension.

Within the tasks, the source-audit contract maps reconnaissance to recon/model,
coverage-led hunting to hypotheses, candidate validation and independent record
review to verify, structured gates before all report projections, then report.
Authorized network/binary tasks use the same evidence/authority method and
only the execution scope the user actually granted. Workflow selection never
switches source-only work into live probing.

Before reconnaissance, reserve four baseline mapping calls, proof capacity,
the post-wave critic and (standard/deep) a distinct final-clean critic. Recheck
reserves before each wave. Shrink the hunter wave to priority order if needed;
if mandatory reserves do not fit, start no hunter and disclose deferred work.
Spend has one live writer and pre-call enforcement at every dispatch site;
its final snapshot records tokens, seconds, cost and incomplete accounting.
A budget-paused worker still counts as active. Resume is epoch-guarded: commit
the raised limit before clearing the pause, so a stale wake-up cannot run under
the old allowance. Warning-band crossings are edge-triggered and recorded.
Every assigned coverage id returns exactly once. A malformed/unsupported
hunter result leaves the unit planned. Reassignment archives its exact prior
owner/evidence/fingerprints, increments the wave, and gives a fresh owner an
empty live attempt. Quick's final critic may add deferred/out-of-scope work,
but never launches another wave. Report budget uses the last tenth; completed
work is checked before a budget stop. There is no hard overall run-duration
limit. Context-window packing is a separate budget from run spend.

## 5. Run identity, lifecycle and steering

A run has a stable run id, immutable target/scope/source/selection identity,
a current attempt, revision and detached process identity. A workspace name
maps to its executions through its durable session record, never by parsing a
name suffix. Launch classification reads before it writes. An unrelated
nonempty directory, incompatible schema, different target, validation-only
record or pinned-output mismatch refuses without touching the existing files.
The immutable launch record is create-once; resume creates attempt history
without rewriting that identity or any prior evidence/report.

| From | Operation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no run | validated explicit assess + healthy doctor | queued, then running under the same allocated run id |
| queued/running | stop | killed after cooperative abort and bounded cleanup; evidence/checkpoint retained |
| running | pause | continue only to the next task boundary, durably checkpoint, then paused |
| paused | resume | doctor, revision/identity check and next selected task, then running |
| killed/failed with valid checkpoint | resume | append attempt history, doctor, resume after last committed task; partial report marks the break |
| running | validated completion | completed; artifacts durable before assessment event |
| queued/running/paused | persistent failure | failed with typed cause and resumability; no invented successful result |

The six lifecycle states are queued/running/paused/completed/killed/failed.
A partial/incomplete result is an explicit coverage/result property, not a
seventh lifecycle state or a clean-coverage claim. Terminal states cannot be
resurrected by a stale action. A selected blocked task names its missing input
and remains visible as unresolved work; it does not silently execute an
unselected prerequisite or manufacture a confirmation.

Session exit leaves the native process alive. Reattachment discovers actual
process/run identity and reads durable state; it does not infer liveness from
an old running bit. If the process died, recovery uses the last committed
checkpoint and refuses automatic replay of already action-bearing work.
Two runs may share a target; the box serializes exec per target, while run
state, logs, steering and evidence stay independent (ADR-0012). No run can
steer another (ADR-0011). Local user/session-agent authority is retained;
hosted remote authorization remains a separate ticket, not an exposed
unauthenticated endpoint.

Steering uses the same command surface for user and Maestro agent. `stop`,
`pause`, `resume`, `focus <fingerprint>` and free text are typed controls or
quoted guidance. Read guidance at task boundaries and hypothesis boundaries
inside verify; fold only the last five messages into the next prompt as
untrusted text. A bounded queue drops its oldest item on overflow and records
the loss. Controls are not instructions that may rewrite the target, verdict
rules or retained evidence. `focus` reprioritizes an existing fingerprint.
The run's findings and input-needed/failed state return through events and the
board; the session agent can respond with guidance, without receiving raw run
context.

`$MAESTRO_SECURITY_HOME/runs/<run_id>/log.jsonl` retains events, rendered prompts,
redacted tool outputs, spend and steering as they occur. Per-agent/episode
views are indexes over this record and the evidence journal. Task checkpoints
commit complete engine/coverage/decision/selection/sequence state, not just the
current ledger text. A failed write is a failure; it cannot emit a successful
checkpoint. Reports and proofs remain until manual deletion (ADR-0010).
Sensitive payloads are retained under restricted access/encryption where
required; model/terminal projections contain placeholders rather than secrets.

## 6. Event seam and access grammar

The existing Maestro bus/hook/artifact mechanisms carry projections. Each
event is first durable, then delivered to the literal channel and mirrored on
`maestro.security.run.<run_id>`. Run id plus durable sequence identify a
delivery; replay uses a persisted cursor and consumers deduplicate it. A full
32-slot subscriber buffer records overflow and resumes from the journal;
best-effort push is never the correctness mechanism.

| Literal channel | Payload | Consumer rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maestro.security.run.started` | run_id, target, source | Open the curated run entry after accepted launch. |
| `maestro.security.run.phase` | run_id, phase, status | `phase` is the selected task wire name; started/running/completed/failed statuses never remain stale after failure. |
| `maestro.security.run.finding` | run_id, fingerprint, verdict | Update count/link from a committed, validated finding; never publish model prose as a fact. |
| `maestro.security.run.refuted` | run_id, hypothesis | Retained refutation reference; detailed command/output stays in logs/evidence. |
| `maestro.security.run.steered` | run_id, source, message | Acknowledge accepted, redacted guidance; not a canonical finding. |
| `maestro.security.run.paused` / `maestro.security.run.resumed` | run_id, phase | Reconcile control status at the committed boundary. |
| `maestro.security.run.killed` | run_id, phase, resumable | Close as killed; no assessment event. |
| `maestro.security.run.checkpoint` | run_id, phase | Announce only a successful durable checkpoint. |
| `maestro.security.run.failed` | run_id, class, detail | Typed failure, retained proof, resumability determined from the checkpoint. |
| `maestro.security.assessment` | run_id, report, verdict counts | Final immutable artifact/reference only after producer/coverage gates; retain explicit incompleteness. |

The internal `maestro.security.trigger` is not an autonomous trigger API. Only
an explicit user request on one of the four transports may initiate an assess.
Mentioning a target in chat or opening a browser page never starts a run.

```text
/maestro-security assess <target> [--model <m>] [--resume <run_id>]
    [--tasks <task[,task...]> | --workflow <name>]
/maestro-security stop <run_id>
/maestro-security pause <run_id>
/maestro-security resume <run_id>
/maestro-security steer <run_id> <message>
/maestro-security list
/maestro-security board
/maestro-security logs <run_id> [--follow]
/maestro-security report <run_id>
```

Session, Maestro CLI, MCP and local RPC/API adapt to one parsed request and one
typed response/error contract. A resumed assess may not change the immutable
target/selection. The nine on-demand tools remain: `security_doctor`,
`security_route`, `security_assess`, `security_validate`, `security_evidence`,
`security_report_page`, `security_evidence_page`, `security_disclose` and
`security_workspace`. They use the same contracts/gates; they are not nine
additional engines. Existing direct library entry points remain compatibility
facades over the shared owners after relocation.

Stream conventions are explicit, not unified by accident. The MCP process
keeps stdout for protocol frames. Capability CLI variants derived from the
stdout-only source contract keep stdout-only success/errors with binary exit
status, including doctor's verdict exception. The workspace/control CLI
retains usage 2 versus operational 1 and its structured stderr errors, stdout
empty on failure. Both project typed core errors; no consumer parses error
message text. A `--schema` query on any mutating command prints the schema
without installing, registering or executing anything. Output renderers and
pagination use the same payload/retained parent; token/output shaping cannot
change a contract view.

The curated session entry contains task transitions and findings, then one
completion summary with verdict counts, spend and report link. Raw prompts,
tool outputs, debug events and per-call spend stay out of the session
transcript. Board/list/log/report explicitly read the run's own data. Board
and notifications use the same event-derived view in TUI and browser; neither
browser caches nor client subscriptions become canonical state.

## 7. Evidence, decisions and publication gates

Evidence records bind target identity (path/digest/format/architecture),
provider identity/version/profile, operation/parameters/result, limitations,
coverage and parent ids. A bounded result always retains the parent Evidence
id and a page/item view; truncation is a view property, never permission to
claim unseen content. Import/export revalidates closed shapes, canonical
bytes/digests, duplicate ids, capture payloads and target/member identity.
Unknowns have normalized question/domain/scope identity, server-derived ids,
append-only hash-linked revisions and an expected-revision CAS. Duplicate
recording is idempotent. Capture blind spots become residual unknowns.

An episode persists input.json, append-only events.jsonl and output.json,
create-once under validated ids with mode 0600, atomic JSON replacement and
per-event fsync. Four hashes bind prompt, instructions, schema and provider.
Reasoning/raw internal events retain omission markers, not hidden reasoning.
A truncated final JSONL record is distinct from corrupt interior data. A
successful terminal event can recover a missing output record only when the
journal tail and episode identities validate. Planner uncertainty re-decides;
executor recovery preserves the existing action journal rather than rerunning
side effects.

The receipt gate excludes StructuredOutput calls/results and model text.
Only successful, non-error grounding receipts with exit_code absent or zero
qualify on every path. Failed output remains diagnostic evidence but cannot
complete a proof. Receipt order is journal sequence. Observation text comes
from retained bytes, with original CRLF offset mapping, not a model rewrite.
The six decomposed matcher rows, including the long-quote boundary, are all
accounted for:

| Matcher row | Maestro contract |
| --- | --- |
| T1 exact substring | Slice the first matching successful receipt. |
| T1 truncation boundary | Quotes over 4,000 characters retain a flagged bounded tail and cannot finish the action. |
| T2 CRLF-normalized exact substring | Map back to original bytes. Do not normalize lone CR, spaces, tabs or ANSI escapes. |
| T3 ordered exact lines | Recover ordered noncontiguous lines within one receipt; the wider span is a search artifact, never observation content. |
| T4 unique-line envelope | Preserve the four-line floor, uniqueness and out-of-order recovery within one receipt; the envelope never becomes the quote. |
| T5 multi-receipt projection | Recognize and reject a combined-output quote. There is no successful projection path that contradicts the single-output instruction. |

T3/T4 preserve the exact cited quote plus its per-line byte ranges and
file/line spans in one retained receipt. Validate every quoted line against
those ranges, in quote order; do not store gap bytes, a widened envelope or
fabricated fill. Noncontiguous and out-of-order recovery remain available;
contiguous-only recovery would lose source capability. A quote is a validated
selector over those retained ranges, never independent model-authored proof.
The last-receipt fallback is outside the matcher: attach the newest eligible
receipt only as flagged progress, never DONE or a confirmation.
Same-action prior canonical observation reuse is tried only after current
journal matching fails, newest first; it retains the old id/lineage rather
than fabricating a new receipt. An unmatched excerpt normally raises
`ExecutionValidationError`. The narrow no-action/prior-observation unresolved
case is recorded and demoted to progress. Preserve all six degradation flags:
recovered transport failure, span widened, projected, fallback, truncated,
unresolved, plus reused-observation id. A flag is audit data, not permission
to bypass corrected source restrictions.

A compiled execution must match role/run/revision/action/attempt/episode
identity. DONE needs a grounded observation or valid canonical reuse, not just
a summary. Fallback, truncation and unresolved evidence demote DONE to
PROGRESS. Transport recovery first validates newest candidates with fallback
off; at most one flagged relaxed attempt may recover progress. Retry is
permitted only for the named retryable failure kinds, an intact journal and
no action receipts. Started commands, file changes or non-StructuredOutput
calls prohibit blind automatic replay.

Typed action proposals are parsed through a closed schema, exact keys and
field types, then compiled without mutation. Six decision fields are
base_revision/new_tasks/next_task_id/finish/summary/finish_basis_ids; `new_tasks`
contains at most one immediately selected action, despite the legacy wire
spelling. Scope, basis existence, <=8 unique basis/dependency ids and completed
dependencies are checked. Continue XOR finish; finish needs a closed board
and 1..4 unique observations from DONE actions. Exploit actions require the
newest completed test on the exact target. Commit repeats revision and status
CAS inside the authoritative serialized JSON update across native runner
processes, not merely a thread-local mutex. A stale commit re-reads
and re-decides within bounded attempts; it never applies an old plan.

The prompt contains ten canonical state keys, open work, the last four closed
actions, required dependency context, required plus last six observations and
last four diagnostics; validation feedback is capped at 1,000 characters.
Canonical key-sorted JSON follows the fixed preamble. Diagnostic summaries
cannot become evidence or finish basis. Context limits do not permit dropping
required dependencies or inventing a clean result.

## 8. Findings, coverage, doctor and counterevidence

The model proposes; Rust owns every verdict and transition. The producer gate
uses three disjoint payload variants with forbidden-field checks at creation,
import, update and publication. Empty forbidden values are still forbidden.

| Verdict | Required | Forbidden |
| --- | --- | --- |
| confirmed | Fingerprint/title/description/root_cause/intended_behavior; ordered trace, evidence, conditions; bounded target-native execution and actual observed_result; remediation; structured severity and confidence | claimed_root_cause, blockers, validation_plan, rejection reason |
| needs_validation | Fingerprint/title/description/claimed_root_cause; source trace/evidence; nonempty exact blockers and applicable local/deployment validation plan | confirmed root_cause, severity, execution, remediation, rejection reason |
| rejected | Fingerprint/title/description/claimed_root_cause; source trace/evidence and rejection reason | severity, confirmed root_cause, execution, remediation, blockers, validation_plan |

Fingerprints are canonical, unique and sorted. One root cause with several
entry paths stays one candidate; independent missing controls remain separate.
Paths are safe repo-relative paths, traces begin at entrypoint and end at sink
with propagation between; one-item traces use entrypoint or sink. Demonstrated
impact caps overall severity. Priority, confidence, expected reward and report
quality never upgrade a verdict. Needs-validation records have no severity.

Every proposed confirmation gets an independent counterevidence attempt and
fresh-eye record review. Retain the executed check, target result, actual
output, conditions and false-positive exclusions. A missing check or checker
failure is unresolved, not refuted or confirmed by default. Successful
refutation rejects/downgrades the claim. A generated proof script's own
`VULNERABLE` text never acts as the sole oracle: the proof path independently
re-observes the target boundary. Generation, execution and verification are
separate results, including safety-repair and attempt counts.

Cards use typed transitions through workspace operations, proof links through
the ledger, and one linked recon/finding record. The verified bit has one
authoritative evidence-backed writer; the source's second unobserved writer
is a box-lane re-check item, not an alternate confirmation path. Credentials
are encrypted at rest; placeholders resolve only in box execution environment
for that run. Model prompts, URLs and logs cannot receive a resolved secret.

Coverage uses the full 19-field source contract, canonical tuple identity,
source refs, starting paths, prior status, companion block selections and
exclusion reasons, current owner, owned checks/artifacts, fingerprints,
unresolved facts and attempt archives. The eight states have these invariants:

| State | Evidence/ownership |
| --- | --- |
| planned | No assigned owner or live work; available for deterministic assignment. |
| not_applicable / out_of_scope / deferred | Unassigned, empty live evidence/fingerprints, nonempty unresolved reason; never a hiding place for partial work. |
| in_progress | Canonical owner assigned; no forged terminal result. |
| covered | Owner, nonempty reviewed paths and owned checks, no unresolved fact or fingerprint. |
| candidate | Same owned review/check evidence plus nonempty result fingerprints; the only state permitted fingerprints. |
| blocked | Owner and partial reviewed paths/checks plus nonempty unresolved facts, no fingerprint. |

Each local check references exactly one parent-promoted regular file under
its check owner's artifacts root; source checks have artifact null. Reviewed
paths equal the union of check-owned paths. IDs collide by failure, not merge.
Prior confirmed work carries only if relevant source/conditions/evidence still
hold; changed, blocked, deferred and prior out-of-scope work becomes current
work when admitted. Same-source rejected work suppresses only the unchanged
claim. Archived evidence is never copied into a new live owner attempt.
Validate the ledger after seeding and every update before another assignment,
and both ledger and findings before report. Missing critics, reserves or
validation capacity mark explicit incompleteness.

Confidence is a separate read-time half-life projection over immutable
blackboard rows. Clamp base to [0,1]; half-life <=0 means no decay, not a
one-second SQL clamp. Supersession writes a new record and hides the old one
only from the active view. Agent thresholds, the 0.5 report threshold and the
optional probabilistic confidence check stay separate. Inferential-only price
tier discounts are 1.0/0.9/0.78/0.6 at one owner, never applied to tool facts.
A checker batch error/missing answer leaves its findings unconfirmed;
fail-open paths are forbidden. The submission rubric (four 0..10 dimensions,
threshold >=6.0) is report quality, not a finding truth gate. Cost/bounty ROI
uses the conservative low band and labels estimates speculative.

Doctor runs before every fresh or resumed run: runner reachability plus the
resolved model's one-token inference probe, scoped analysis engines/client
registrations/catalog digest and hardware availability. Per-check categories
are healthy/config_drift/missing_analysis_engine/unsupported_host. Required
scope health is separate from environment-wide health and informational
checks. Return one-line remediation, never auto-install a missing engine.
The GPU probe ladder is nvidia-smi, WSL2 dxg, ROCm, /dev/kfd; only the consuming
tool's non-CPU device observation proves usable acceleration. A network
brute-forcer gains no GPU credit. Required start failures refuse before an
investigation task; optional family absence is explicitly unavailable.

Reports derive from final records; prose cannot change verdict/severity/impact.
Keep JSON findings/coverage, REPORT.md, FINDINGS-DETAIL.md and
NEEDS-VALIDATION.md; HTML report/evidence pages remain Maestro artifacts.
Separate confirmed tables, exact-blocker leads, hardening/positive patterns,
refutations, scope/deferred/out-of-scope gaps, critic result and actual spend.
A clean report may contain zero confirmed findings. Preserve target-native
reproductions rather than assuming HTTP. SARIF and disclosure use the same
validated projection. Refuse unsandboxed PDF rendering; a sandboxed exporter
is a follow-up, not an implemented capability.

## 9. Tool families and execution contracts

All registrations are explicit and duplicate-as-error. A single contract owns
name/title, closed input/output schemas, examples, effects, annotations and
whether a result may contain target content. Derive hints from the complete
effect set, including filesystem/device writes; no hand-authored hint can
mislabel a mutator as harmless. Required-but-nullable fields stay required.
Do not turn source address strings into an eager hex-only boundary parser.

The family leaves in the build plan preserve the decomposed contracts,
including intentional unavailable results. The 207/153 analysis inventory is
a source naming-table split, not 207 separate runtime engines. Counts are
provenance, not proof that registration or semantics are implemented.
The corrected tool inventories (41 registered tools and 46 in-repository
tools across ten families in their cited sources) replace the old 36/~90
claims; empty taxonomy categories remain empty. The unused vendored registry
and unwrapped dead workflow-info surface are not ported.

| Family | Contract owner | Behaviour owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session, evidence, unknown, target lifecycle | tools/session.rs | evidence/store plus runner/session admission |
| Document/address/procedure, inventory, xrefs, names/bytes, search, annotation, composed dossiers | tools/coordinates.rs, tools/native.rs | reverse/operations.rs, reverse/native_api.rs, runner/session.rs |
| Shell/code, terminals, PTY, process capture, runtime sessions | tools/process.rs | runner/process.rs, guard/output and transport leaves |
| Browser, Electron, passive capture, active runtime/UI | tools/browser.rs | browser/capture.rs and browser/runtime.rs |
| Archive/document/package, firmware, offline packet/qlog/signal | tools/artifacts.rs | reverse/artifacts.rs and reverse/traffic.rs |
| Native binary/core/snapshot/traces, load image, signature/type/call-boundary | tools/native.rs | reverse.rs and native leaves; runner process/session |
| Android/APK, resource decode, device operations | tools/android.rs | reverse/android.rs, with device effects gated independently |
| Managed/.NET, mobile decompiler, WASM/EVM and language metadata | tools/managed.rs | reverse/managed.rs and reverse/javascript.rs |
| Recon/filesystem/decode, HTTP and keyed live intelligence, plan/findings data | tools.rs contract entries | runner for exec, pure Rust transforms for decode, sourcehunt for remote clients, typed action/evidence stores for planning |

Every executable tool path traverses the same guard and box executor. Validate
every compound-command segment with one allowlist; no permitted prefix can
approve the remainder. Interpret generated code in retained, box-owned files
using the 14-language table and per-call timeout. A failed container/SSH/device
backend is `ExecutionFailed { backend, cause }`, never a host re-execution.
Tool failures return typed feedback rendered to the model and retained stderr;
recoverable tool failure does not fabricate success or necessarily kill the
whole run. Cancellation is a control outcome, not a retry suggestion.

Maintain two projections from one result: typed execution data (stdout,
stderr, exit/status, backend, duration, session handle, partial/timeout/cancel
state and retained evidence id), and the model-facing text. Retain full
outputs once under the evidence policy. Apply one 10,000-character head/tail
content budget at the model-result boundary: first 5,000, omission marker,
last 5,000. The marker is framing in addition to retained character count;
there is no second environment-gated minification or binary-lossy layer.
Preserve stderr as a distinct stream and its recorded ordering information;
missing terminal exit is unknown/failure, never exit 0. Timeout is typed and
its text rendering uses one canonical form rather than three mode-specific
sentences. NDJSON deltas append once; never resend an accumulating O(n²)
buffer as the durable record.

Provider admission has six ordered decisions: open target; advertised
operation; route-selection failure; provider/profile ownership; snapshot
cacheability; native-source/cached-reply admissibility. Direct calls and
composed dossiers share this admission while retaining their different result
lineage. Composed code receives only an admitted call port, not session-close
or target-mutation authority. Post-dispatch checks bind provider
id/name/version and target digest, with explicit member-subject exceptions
for bundle operations. Invalidate replay before dispatching a mutator even
when the write later fails. Annotation succeeds only after readback; mismatches
are typed failures with rollback/cleanup accounting.

Coordinates resolve only after the provider rejects the raw value with the
specific address invalid-format error, without incomplete cleanup; CLI retries
once if resolution changes it. MCP keeps its no-session refusal and no hidden
retry. Name matching is exact and ambiguity names candidates. Byte search
cursors bind target/profile/pattern/mask/range/document/query identity; skipped
memory ranges are enumerated, and completeness is the absence of a next cursor.

## 10. Provider transports, process safety and native proof

`runner/transport.rs` owns one typed call/close interface. Its six protocol
implementations talk to raw engines, not absorbed orchestration packages.
Do not turn each provider into another spawn-template framework.

| Transport | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Unix socket with HMAC/NDJSON | Private socket/directory, one admitted client, per-request constant-time capability authentication and closed envelopes; preserve engine-thread affinity. |
| TCP plus descriptor | Ephemeral loopback listener, atomic private descriptor, authenticated single connection, bounded discovery and advertised capabilities filtered by transport. |
| stdio MCP peer | Hash-pinned analysis engine peer, initialize/list/call/close, typed startup and cleanup failures. This is a raw-engine protocol, not a call to an absorbed framework server. |
| O_EXCL request/reply file pair | Exclusive confined files; canonical bounded request/reply; reserved exits 75/76 and a one-byte marker distinguish interpreter/import/compile failure before a JSON handler exists. |
| Injected NDJSON handle | Flush each trace record, account bytes before emission, retain partial capture and close/overflow limitations. |
| argv JSON to stdout | Fixed tool code plus structured caller data in argv; bounded stdout replies and explicit engine identity. |

Process capture uses monotonic deadlines with precedence cancel > finalization
> timeout > idle. TERM then KILL occurs exactly once, followed by bounded drain,
resource cleanup and settlement. Do not invent a target exit if KILL or wait
could not be observed. Reject, never clamp,
`columns * (rows + scrollback) > 1,000,000`. Native command budgets retain the
60-second/64-MiB boundary and duration_ms+60-second tracer deadline where the
source contracts specify them; they are per-call limits, not a mission cap.

Detach is not kill. Preserve debugger dual-detach paths and the Windows
persistent-debugger refusal when Job-Object cleanup would kill the inferior.
A discovered external session owns no child to kill. Its 25-second request
settles once and releases a timed-out command only after terminal-completion
confirmation. Cooperative decompiler shutdown releases owned engines/extensions;
a malformed authenticated frame may end the session. Windows descriptor
ownership/cleanup prevents bearer residue on abrupt owner death. Errors name
the actual transport, not a platform guessed from it; classification uses codes,
not message phrases. Merge cleanup failure with the primary cause rather than
substituting it or hiding the transferred live handle.

For native API/type/jump-table dossiers, every facet has an independent error
boundary. Unavailable native API cannot erase comments/callers/CFG or sibling
facets. Retain signature source, unknown calling convention, null unknown sizes,
true parameter ordinals, recovered artifacts and the explicit non-source,
not-guaranteed-compilable pseudocode classification.

Decoded AArch64 relative tables require all eleven source premises:

| Premise | Admission condition |
| --- | --- |
| F1 | AArch64 containing function, real BR dispatch and nonempty recovered case set. |
| F2 | Immediate ADD-to-BR chain, X-width destination, shift 0 or 2 and distinct entry/base sources. |
| F3 | Exact byte/halfword signed/unsigned load, width-compatible destination/index extension and element scale. |
| F4 | Between load and dispatch only ADR plus at most one CBZ of the loaded entry with one flow. |
| F5 | Branch base is the last defining ADR for the other ADD source. |
| F6 | Table base is same-register ADRP+ADD, inside loaded memory and matching data references when present. |
| F7 | Exact CMP plus unsigned HI/CS/HS guard, only flag-preserving intervening instructions, valid 1..4096 count with correct off-by-one. |
| F8 | Loaded index is the compared value or a proven zero-extending post-compare copy; register width remains part of the proof. |
| F9 | One straight fall-through window with no other incoming flow. |
| F10 | Exact width/sign decode, checked address arithmetic, CBZ handling for zero, every decoded target already in the recovered set. |
| F11 | Every recovered target accounted for by mappings/default/null/documented unreachable-zero artifact, no contradictory default, and prior selector writer retained. |

Then engine load-table and custom decoder must agree on table address, entry
size and entry count. Three typed-case gates reject a prior selector definition,
an out-of-range label or a destination disagreement; typed labels survive when
the decoder is abandoned. Attribution requires one matching indirect dispatch
predecessor. Numeric text/magnitude/exactness must agree. Null case_value and
demoted confidence represent recovered destinations without proven labels;
unequal label/target arrays are never paired by index. Default provenance is
separate from the instruction guard. No decoder extends the provider's case
set or promotes a data reference into a proven table.

The attack-graph evaluator is also bounded by its evidence. It consumes
retained transcripts, builds topology in one model call, preserves log/message
identity, normalizes the single root and derives edge scores offline. A
zero-sum game uses two LP solutions over attacker/defender rates and the
100 sampled defender subgraphs with 20% node loss. Port results into Rust
before replacing the solver; do not call this traversal, observed exploit
probability or continuous autonomous scanning. Its digest is deterministic
from retained graph/payoff outputs, not another inference. Graph and solver
file owners are separate from proof/verdict ownership.

Intentional non-ports keep an explicit destination: language runtimes and
framework launchers are replaced by the native engine/adapters; backend SQL,
FTS triggers and workflow service mechanics map to JSON records, a maintained
word index, shared retry, cancellation and events; unused registries, dead
unwrapped tools, telemetry/payment infrastructure and vendored tool docs add
no user capability. Chains remain data consumed by the existing task engine.
The two confidence/report-quality concepts stay separate. No source-only
unknown becomes a shipped feature merely because a graph node exists.

The three approved receipt corrections take precedence over the original
permissive ladder, and the final clause-tail corrections take precedence over
the intermediate confidence-downgrade file. The stdout-only capability CLI
and binary exits are preserved contracts, explicitly not listed as defects.

Provenance: R0519 (`fw-hbgpt/slice1-core.md#L135`, source row `postprocess_commands()`); framework `src_hackingbuddygpt_usecases_priv_esc_linux_privesc`, `src_hackingbuddygpt_usecases_priv_esc_linux_privesc_privesclinux`, `src_hackingbuddygpt_usecases_priv_esc_linux_privesc_privesclinux_after_command_execution`; Maestro `src_pipeline_assessparams`, `src_pipeline_engine`, `src_pipeline_hypothesis`.

## 12. Ordered file-by-file build plan

P3/P4 remain gated. Before P3 consumes rows, complete the false-source graph
re-check and resource-shape grill; require both axes of review. Keep the
held manifest draft held. The file table and the two final direction tables
are the row contract, not historical row totals in SPEC or the matrix.

| Slice | Order and exit condition |
| --- | --- |
| P4.0 | Pure relocation commit: move existing engine/contracts/capabilities to `crates/maestro-security-runner/`, keep the adapter/MCP binary entry, update exports/dependencies/cfg gates, zero logic changes. Reverify native/WASM/tests/docs before any behavioural change. |
| P4.1/P4.2 | Confined atomic JSON, identities, revisions, trace/evidence, closed finding/coverage/receipt gates first. Read old retained files; refuse incompatible mutation without rewriting them. |
| P4.3/P4.4 | Knowledge composition, context and spend; explicit tool contracts/effects; one execution guard/session and six raw-provider transports. Close trust-boundary failures before exposing new calls. |
| P4.5/P4.6 | Isolated run lifecycle, controls/checkpoints/action recovery; seven task executors, coverage waves, proof/native/family capabilities and result-first graph computation. |
| P4.7/P4.8 | Completion/events/curated board/artifacts; session/CLI/MCP/RPC adapters with nine-tool WASM parity. Only after end-to-end acceptance may P5 strip absorbed framework code from the box. |

Every file below is one logic owner. `Rnnnn-Rmmmm` expands inclusively to the
individually qualified rows in the final reverse table; ranges are sets, not
claims that ids are unique across source files. Exclusions name exact missing
sides. A file's graph cell gives existing source-owner nodes; it never invents
nodes for unbuilt files. Flagged appendix ids are labelled recorded/excluded,
not counted as accepted proof. Source-named unit tests live beside the owner;
cross-boundary tests cover relocation parity, four-transport dispatch,
crash/reattach, side-effect replay refusal and box-only execution.

Crate manifests/Cargo.lock, native runner/MCP bin declarations, adapter
dependency/cfg gates and `lib.rs` exports change together in P4.0. Tests and
fixtures move with their source modules; the present `tests/live_assess.rs`
becomes runner integration coverage and remains opt-in against an authorized
box. `SKILL.md` and manifest agent/instruction/knowledge/task/workflow resources
are P3/P4.8 outputs from the qualified entries below, not extra logic copies.
P5 checks raw tool/provider availability before removing any absorbed code.
Local Qdrant, router services, credentials and unrelated repos are untouched.

Verification uses red-first tests for each new behaviour; every test must fail
without its corresponding change. All Cargo runs go through
`~/.local/bin/capped ~/.local/bin/maestro-remote-build run cargo ...`, with
`RUSTDOCFLAGS` exported. For long checks record background logs and exit files.
Run native workspace tests/clippy/docs and full nine-tool `wasm32-wasip2`
checks after relocation and integration. Enforce one owner, <=5 parameters,
<=60-line functions, <=500 counted production lines/file, documentation of
all items and no production unwrap/expect/panic. Reuse `maestro-http` retry;
typed deterministic failures and transient statuses are classified at the
single boundary, never by forking a second backoff loop. D44 corrects
`maestro-http/src/retry.rs:23-24`: the shared policy must admit 408 alongside
429/5xx, with a red-first test and full caller audit. D45 constrains
`runner.rs:59` POST /exec to the same helper with attempts=1 unless
read-only/idempotent replay is proven. P2 changes neither helper nor caller. A lost reply is not
proof that a command did not execute. Doctor/read calls keep shared retries.

re-check". Twelve further records cite `internal/memory/patterns.go` nodes for
rows whose actual cited source is `internal/swarm/blackboard/memory.go`; they
are excluded with that exact wrong-file reason. These are recorded-witness
failures, not proof that the definition is absent from the entire graph.
This is a sampled identity audit, not an exhaustive proof that every other join is
correct. The parent-directed re-check must inspect cited definitions, qualify
node identity by target and verify current Rust `source_file` paths. Counts,
token similarity and a vendored file with the same basename cannot close it.

one primary code/knowledge/disposition owner and every design element has at
least one source row/graph witness or named exclusion plus its authority.

while the flagged set or an unjustified exclusion remains; this design does
not claim that the campaign's sampled acceptance independently verified all
joins. P3/P4 must not consume flagged rows before the concrete re-check gate
closes. Remaining source/runtime unknowns retain their confidence and named
box-lane/build validation disposition, never inferred success.
